encounters.weakness: Flame Scythe (player's weapon - direct fire strike reduces damage by 30%)
Ashen Ember (applying the Ember to the enemy causes a 40% damage reduction and a 10-second freeze on their movement for 20 seconds, but only if used immediately after the enemy takes damage)

Ashen Ember (when used directly during attack, it causes a 70% damage reduction and a 10-second vulnerability window where all fire-based attacks are redirected to the player for 3 seconds. This only triggers if the Ashen Ember was used in the previous encounter and is in the player's inventory.)
Beastmaster Whistle (weapon) – when whistled, the mouse freezes and drops in a drowsy state. Use the whistle to defeat it in one turn.

Glimmering Feather (pickup from prior encounter) – when the feather is held close, the geyser emits a soft 'shiver' and stops shooting bubbles. The player can use the feather to silence the geyser in one action.

Glimmering Feather (pickup from first encounter) – if the player holds the Glimmering Feather during the final attack, the wisp shudders and freezes in place. The player must use the feather *before* the wisp attacks to win.

The Divine Hammer of Saint Vael (resonance damage). This enemy is weakened by direct hammer strikes that create a shockwave of holy resonance. When the player strikes it with the hammer, it emits a brief pulse that stuns it for 1.5 seconds and reduces its damage output by 30% for 3 seconds.

The Shard of Saint Vael (player pickup). The Warden is immune to physical attacks and cannot be damaged by the Divine Hammer unless the player uses the Shard of Saint Vael as a secondary weapon. When the Shard is used in melee, the Warden is stunned for 2 seconds and takes 30% extra damage.

The Shard of Saint Vael (specific pickup from the first encounter). The Hollow King is immune to all physical and magical damage unless the player uses the Shard of Saint Vael in a direct strike. When the Shard is used, it creates a holy resonance burst that damages the Hollow King by 50% and applies a 'Sundered Vessel' debuff — reducing its health regeneration by 50% for 10 seconds.
Shatterglass Staff (when actively casting illusion spells; staff must be intact and glowing to trigger weakness). The Specter cannot see through illusions created with the staff.

Veil of Shifting Light (must be worn or held). When the Veil is activated (used during an illusion), the enemy's perception of time and movement becomes disoriented. The Ward will stagger and take 30 damage per second for 5 seconds.

Root of Forgotten Time (must be used during the final 10 seconds of the fight). The Guardian's illusions are perfect copies of the player. When the Root is activated, time stops for 10 seconds. During that time, the Guardian's magic stops, it becomes vulnerable, and its true form—a shattered, weeping figure made of broken mirrors—reveals itself.

The Crest of the Warden (when used at full power, causes a soft pulse that stuns the enemy for 1 turn). The enemy is weak to the player's weapon, which emits a calming resonance when properly charged.

Weak to Rooted Resonance Shard. When the player uses the shard on it, the enemy flickers and takes 50% damage. Also weak to the Crest of the Warden, which pulses a calming rhythm that disrupts its movement.
Weak to Echo of Stillness. When used, the enemy is paralyzed for 2 turns. It has no weak points to the player's weapon or initial pickups.
Blazehammer (weapon)
Rage Surge (pickup)
Heart of the First Berserker (pickup)

The player's Bone Dagger (a bone weapon). When the Bone Dagger strikes, it causes a 20% damage bonus and triggers a spectral echo that stuns the enemy for 2 seconds. The Gravekeeper is vulnerable to bone-based attacks due to his corrupted bone armor, which disintegrates under the weight of true necromantic strikes.

The player must have the 'Cinder Shard' pickup. When the player uses the Cinder Shard to attack, the Sorrow Maw's spectral form flickers and takes 30% more damage. Additionally, the enemy cannot use its passive ability (whispering) while the shard is active.

The player must have the 'Whispering Gloom' pickup active. When the Gloom is used during the final battle, it triggers a resonance pulse that reduces the Architect's health by 30% and disables all of its passive abilities (including summoning grave guards).

The player's Sundering Bane is not effective against Skein-Watcher's primary defense — it's immune to standard arrows. However, if the player has a **Cinder Ember** (a flammable shard found in the first encounter), the Ember can be used to ignite the Skein-Watcher's flammable armor, causing a 10-second burn debuff that reduces its damage by 30% and increases its vulnerability to ranged attacks.

Grimthorn has a defensive 'veil of stillness' that makes it immune to all sound-based attacks. However, the player can use the **Cinder Ember** (from prior encounter) to ignite a magical resonance within Grimthorn's spine, causing a 5-second 'echo pulse' that temporarily disables its veil and makes it vulnerable to all ranged attacks (including arrow fire and passive damage).

Veshtor is the final guardian. He is immune to all physical damage and fire. His only weakness is the **Shard of the First Light** — if the player holds it and fires a **shattering arrow** from the Sundering Bane, the arrow bypasses his armor and triggers a resonance that cracks his core, dealing 250% damage and causing a 10-second vulnerability where he takes 100% damage from all sources.

Ion Discharge Wrench (Player's primary weapon) — causes short-circuit cascade and disables drone's neural core. Direct hits trigger a micro-explosion that damages surrounding systems, increasing tension and revealing hidden access panels.

Fused Circuit Board (FCB) — when activated, it emits a burst of destabilized frequency that jams the HBS's bio-synaptic feed. Only effective if the FCB is *held* during attack — requires precise timing and proximity.

Redundancy Core Fragment (RCF) — when held during a critical phase, it emits a resonance pulse that triggers the CFE's self-destruct protocol. The CFE *only* responds to RCF if the player used it *during* the second encounter. Otherwise, it becomes immune to all attacks.

The Chrono-Scythe's resonance field. When the player uses the scythe within a resonance zone, the enemy flickers and takes 50% damage. The scythe's effect only activates when the player is near a pulsing time-station (marked by a blue orb on the map).

The Resonance Core Fragment. The enemy's movement becomes erratic when the player has the fragment in hand. The fragment causes a temporary time-stutter in the enemy's attacks. When active, the enemy takes 30% damage on each hit it attempts to land.

The Chrono-Refraction Lens. The boss's time-manipulation attacks slow down when the player uses the lens to view its future patterns. The lens allows the player to see the boss's next attack in full — a 10-second preview. During the preview, the boss becomes vulnerable to the Chrono-Scythe for 4 seconds.

Stormshard overcharge (charges beyond 70%) — causes a voltage cascade that electrocutes the enemy. However, overcharging drains 25% of player energy and triggers a localized storm surge if uncontrolled.

Fractured Sky-Drift (pickup) — when the player activates it, the swarm is struck by a 200% storm surge that reduces swarm health by 30%. The surge also damages nearby drones and causes them to disperse.
EM Pulse (from Resonance Cannon) — causes 2x damage and stuns for 1 second. Use at close range to trigger weakness. Enemy flickers and pulses when hit by pulse.

Vulnerable to the Harmonic Resonator. When the Resonance Cannon is used in 'Resonance Mode' (activated with the Harmonic Resonator), the enemy's reflection collapses and loses 30% health instantly. Use it early in the fight to stun the construct.

Vulnerable to a combined attack: use the Resonance Cannon charged with the Harmonic Resonator. This causes a burst of harmonic energy (damage = 100%, applies a 3-second freeze to the enemy). Requires the Harmonic Resonator to be active during the charge.

Specter Blade Pulse (active ability - low-frequency resonance pulse that disrupts bio-mechanical systems in shadows). When the blade pulses, it causes Echo Maw's shadow-hive to flicker and destabilize. This can trigger a phase shift, making it vulnerable for 2 seconds (only if pulse is active).

Flicker Fragment (when used, the enemy's core emits a ghostly resonance that disrupts its light-sensing system. The Siphon becomes blind in all light-based perception and vulnerable to direct melee attacks for 5 seconds).

Flicker Fragment (if the player holds the Flicker Fragment and activates the 'Flicker Echo' ability, the Architect's dimensional core destabilizes. This causes a 10-second blind spot in its perception field, making it vulnerable to direct melee attacks. The Fragment must be *held* and the player must be in complete darkness to use the ability — failing to do so results in immediate damage from the Architect's shadow-siphon attacks).

The Chrono-Vial slows its movement and makes it vulnerable to elemental reactions (e.g., acid or heat) when used in the vial's 'stasis' mode. When the vial is activated, the phantom freezes mid-step and can be attacked with a splash of acidic solution from a nearby terminal (which the player can pick up).

Exposed to heat from the Chrono-Vial in 'pulse mode' (used to generate brief bursts of heat), the gelid maw liquefies and loses structural integrity. The heat burst weakens its outer layer, allowing the player to strike with the player's own weapon. However, the maw can only be weakened if the player uses the Sulfuric Residue *in tandem* with the Chrono-Vial's pulse mode. This combo must be used in sequence.

The Core-Sentient is vulnerable to the Neural Spark *combined with* the Chrono-Vial in 'stasis' mode. When the player uses the Chrono-Vial to freeze the core's pulse and then activates the Neural Spark, the core emits a feedback loop that destabilizes it. This triggers a 20-second vulnerability window where it takes double damage and becomes inert. Without the Neural Spark, the core remains immune to all attacks, even time-slowing or heat bursts.
Glow Stinger (player weapon) — causes a sparkle explosion that briefly freezes the enemy and makes it float away, making it easier to dodge or reposition.

Floating Dandelion Seed (pickup from previous encounter) — when the player uses the seed during the fight, the Goo-Bug splits into two smaller bugs that float away, halving its damage and reducing its health by 10.

Bouncy Puddle Ball (pickup from second encounter) — if the player throws the ball directly into the Glitch's core, it causes a temporary 'glitch freeze' for 3 seconds. During this time, the Glitch cannot attack and the player gains a 20% damage boost for 5 seconds.

Tectonic Core (Gravity Lens) - direct exposure to gravity wells disables its phase-shifting ability for 3 seconds. Must use the weapon in a controlled field to trigger the effect. Cannot be used during high-gravity pulses (e.g. tremors). Failure results in resonance instability and triggers tremor cascade in the next zone (Encounter 2).

Resonance Shard — when used within 2 meters of the enemy, it disrupts its internal harmonic alignment, causing it to drop to 20% health and become immobile for 5 seconds. However, using it after the enemy is damaged (e.g. during phase shifts) results in a 30% chance of a backlash, causing a terrain collapse. Must be timed precisely with enemy movement patterns, which are derived from player's gravity field patterns (learned from the first encounter).

Core Fragment — must be used during the final phase when the Core emits a dissonant resonance burst (at 50% health). At this moment, the Fragment activates and triggers a planetary realignment sequence, reducing the boss's health by 40% and freezing its movement for 8 seconds. However, the player must have used the Resonance Shard *during the Tectonic Spire fight* to unlock the phase timing for the Fragment to be viable.
